definition: Training on pairs of preferred and dispreferred outputs rather than on a scalar reward, used by three sources to install a behaviour and by one to question the signal itself. One feeds the model's own self-certainty into the preference objective so confident answers compress and uncertain ones keep deliberating. One builds pairs from model-generated counterfactual reasoning traces to unlearn knowledge from the CoT as well as the answer, iterating to increase divergence from the original model. One forms pairs by pruning non-essential reasoning segments. The fourth undercuts the common source of preference labels, finding LLM-judge preferences track style rather than safety, world knowledge or instruction following.

evidence.note: Scores unlabeled reasoning trajectories by how their mean-pooled hidden states connect to correct and incorrect reference point clouds built from a small labeled set, and uses that score to pick the concrete chosen and rejected responses inside answer clusters that self-consistency has already separated.
evidence.title: Cloud-ScPO: Hidden-State Geometry for Semi-Supervised Preference Optimization in LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Feeds a reasoning model's own self-certainty into preference optimization so it compresses confident answers and keeps deliberating on uncertain ones.
evidence.title: CAT: Confidence-Adaptive Thinking for Efficient Reasoning of Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Reframes unlearning in reasoning models as an intervention on the CoT itself, having the model generate logically valid counterfactual traces and iteratively preference-tuning toward them.
evidence.title: CiPO: Counterfactual Unlearning for Large Reasoning Models through Iterative Preference Optimization

evidence.note: Prunes chain-of-thought segments the model's own likelihood landscape marks as extraneous, then trains on the resulting pruning preference pairs.
evidence.title: Your Reasoning Model Knows What Counts: Self-Guided Chain-of-Thought Pruning for Efficient Reasoning

evidence.note: Builds a large standardized meta-benchmark and finds that LLM-judge preference scores do not correlate with concrete measures of safety, world knowledge or instruction following, because judges systematically prioritize style over factuality and safety.
evidence.title: Style Outweighs Substance: Failure Modes of LLM Judges in Alignment Benchmarking

name: preference optimization
